properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 993085 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: INTRACOASTAL ENVIRONMENTAL LLC
properties.content:
Report Details

Incident Time: 2011-10-19 22:30:00
Nearest City: Jacksonville Fl, FL
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: OIL: DIESEL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: INTRACOASTAL ENVIRONMENTAL LLC
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 30.337138, -81.654838 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Reported Spill Volume: 25 gallons
Report Description
M/V ALBATROSS IV ALONGSIDE LAYBERTH AT NORTH FLORIDA SHIPYARDS, JACKSONVILLE, FL. RECEIVING DIESEL FUEL DELIVERY/TRANSFER FROM 2 SHORESIDE TANK TRUCKS. DECLARATION OF SECURITY AND FUEL TRANSFER PROCEDURES WERE AGREED UPON, CHIEF ENGR ON DUTY WITH 4 CREWMEMBERS STANDING BY ASSISTING. IT WAS OBSERVED THAT FUEL BEGAN TO LEAK OUT OF ONE OF THE TRUCKS AND OPERATIONS WERE IMMEDIATELY SHUTDOWN. CONTAINMENT ABSORBENT PADS WERE RUN OUT AND A SMALL AMOUNT OF DIESEL DROOLED OVER THE EDGE OF THE DOCK INTO THE ST. JOHNS RIVER (APPROX 5GALS) IN MY ESTIMATION THE ENTIRE SPILL WAS APPROX. 20-25 GALS. TOTAL. THE FACT THAT THE ABSORBENT PADS AND BOOM WERE AVAILABLE KEPT IT FROM REACHING THE WATER IN GREATER VOLUME. I WAS UP IN THE VESSELS WHEELHOUSE AND BECAME AWARE OF THE INCIDENT @ APPROX 1730 EDST. AFTER MAKING CERTAIN THAT ALL TRANSFER OPERATIONS WERE SHUTDOWN AND WOULD NOT CONTINUE, I REPORTED THIS INCIDENT TO JACKSONVILLE USCG SECTOR AND WAS TRANSFERRED TO NRC

Incident Type: MOBILE

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 30.337138, -81.654838 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Reported Spill Volume: 25 gallons
Report Description
M/V ALBATROSS IV ALONGSIDE LAYBERTH AT NORTH FLORIDA SHIPYARDS, JACKSONVILLE, FL. RECEIVING DIESEL FUEL DELIVERY/TRANSFER FROM 2 SHORESIDE TANK TRUCKS. DECLARATION OF SECURITY AND FUEL TRANSFER PROCEDURES WERE AGREED UPON, CHIEF ENGR ON DUTY WITH 4 CREWMEMBERS STANDING BY ASSISTING. IT WAS OBSERVED THAT FUEL BEGAN TO LEAK OUT OF ONE OF THE TRUCKS AND OPERATIONS WERE IMMEDIATELY SHUTDOWN. CONTAINMENT ABSORBENT PADS WERE RUN OUT AND A SMALL AMOUNT OF DIESEL DROOLED OVER THE EDGE OF THE DOCK INTO THE ST. JOHNS RIVER (APPROX 5GALS) IN MY ESTIMATION THE ENTIRE SPILL WAS APPROX. 20-25 GALS. TOTAL. THE FACT THAT THE ABSORBENT PADS AND BOOM WERE AVAILABLE KEPT IT FROM REACHING THE WATER IN GREATER VOLUME. I WAS UP IN THE VESSELS WHEELHOUSE AND BECAME AWARE OF THE INCIDENT @ APPROX 1730 EDST. AFTER MAKING CERTAIN THAT ALL TRANSFER OPERATIONS WERE SHUTDOWN AND WOULD NOT CONTINUE, I REPORTED THIS INCIDENT TO JACKSONVILLE USCG SECTOR AND WAS TRANSFERRED TO NRC

properties.content:

Nearest City: LA
Location: THUNDERHORSE
Incident Type: PLATFORM
Material: TELLUS PLUS OIL 46
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: BP
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 28.190833, -88.495833 (Explicit)
Report Description
WHILE RECOVERING THE FAST RESCUE CRAFT POST LAUNCH AND DRILL, THE CREW MEMBERS ON DECK NOTICED A MINOR LEAK COMING FROM BELOW THE CONTROL BOX SECTION UNDERNEATH THE PDQ. THERE WAS “NO SHEEN” SPOTTED ON THE SURFACE OF THE WATER. THE OIM AND HSE WERE NOTIFIED OF DROPS INTO THE GOM, BUT FURTHER INVESTIGATION WAS NEEDED TO DETERMINE THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK AND WHAT THE FLUID CONSISTED OF. TODAY THE ROPE ABSAILORS WERE ABLE TO SAFELY WORK OVER THE HANDRAIL AND UNDER THE PDQ TO IDENTIFY THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK. THE “TUBING” BETWEEN THE ACCUMULATOR AND THE WINCH BREAK RELEASE LOCATED UNDER THE FRC CONTROL BOX WAS CORRODED AND A MINOR LEAK OF HYDRAULIC OIL DEVELOPED DURING THE WINCH OPERATIONS AND STOPPED ONCE OPERATION WAS COMPLETED.
